name: Latvia

facts.religion: Lutheran about 20%, Catholic about 20%, Orthodox about 18%, many unaffiliated

snapshot: Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs's United List won a record 42 of 100 seats in the October 2026 election, as a party opposed to aiding Ukraine also gained.
culture: Latvia's Song and Dance Festival, held every five years, is a huge national event and, along with the dainas, short folk songs, was key to the "Singing Revolution". Midsummer, Jāņi, is the most important holiday, with bonfires and wreaths. Riga has Europe's largest collection of Art Nouveau buildings.
society: About a quarter of the population is ethnic Russian, and the government has phased out Russian-language schooling. Latvia spends heavily on defence and has reintroduced conscription. Emigration has shrunk the population since 1991. Forestry, logistics and IT are key sectors.
situation: Andris Kulbergs of the centre-right United List became prime minister in May 2026. In the 3 October 2026 election, his party won 42 of 100 seats with about 35 percent, the best result for any party since independence. He is expected to form a new coalition that excludes Sovereign Power, a party opposed to military aid to Ukraine.
power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the majority in the 100-seat Saeima; the president is elected by parliament.

leaders.gov: Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs (United List), since May 2026
